key_insight: Vision-Language-Action models often ignore instruction intent and default to vision-driven shortcuts; this paper systematically measures those 'counterfactual failures' and introduces targeted interventions to make VLAs obey language more faithfully.
problem_solved: VLAs fail to ground language instructions when scene cues or dataset biases encourage repeated, well-learned visual behaviors—leading robots to act on what they expect to see rather than what the instruction requires.
method: Define and quantify 'counterfactual failures' with a focused evaluation protocol and metrics that reveal when behavior is driven by vision shortcuts rather than language.
Perform diagnostic experiments across tasks/datasets to expose bias patterns (e.g., frequent-object selection, repeated actions) and identify failure modes.
Mitigate failures via targeted interventions such as counterfactual data augmentation, rebalancing training examples, and training objectives/regularizers that strengthen language grounding.
impact: Provides practitioners with concrete tools to detect and reduce vision-driven bias in language-grounded control, improving reliability and safety of robot behavior and language grounding in multimodal models.

paper_title: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs
paper_authors: Yu Fang, Yuchun Feng, Dong Jing, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang
